sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, one word or phrase, match).

questions.q: Why was the ancient trade route known as the Silk Route? Give two reasons.
questions.answer: Because silk was one of the chief commodities carried from China, and traders, scholars and missionaries travelled this route.

or.q: How did Indian culture reach Japan?
or.answer: Through Korea: in AD 552 the Korean emperor sent a Buddha statue, sutras, and artists, sculptors, painters and architects to the Japanese emperor.

questions.q: Answer in a phrase: Why are the written syllables and mantras called Shittan in Japanese?
questions.answer: Shittan is believed to be Siddham, the script that gives siddhi (accomplishment).

questions.q: Answer in a phrase: Why are the people of Vietnam called 'Cham'?
questions.answer: Because Champa (Vietnam) was ruled by Indian-origin kings and its people are the Cham.

questions.q: Why was the reign of Emperor Ming Ti significant for the growth of Buddhism in China? Give two reasons.
questions.answer: He invited the Indian monks Kashyapa Matanga and Dharmarakshita in AD 67, and Buddhism entered China through them.

questions.q: Answer in a phrase: (a) Who sent Kashyapa Matanga? (b) When did they go to China?
questions.answer: (a) Emperor Ming Ti invited them. (b) AD 67.

questions.q: Mark true or false: (a) Sri Lanka was the first country to embrace Buddhism abroad. (b) Pali is the literary language of Japan.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False – Pali is the literary language of Sri Lanka.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: Sundo entered Korea in AD ______. The ______ Route carried Buddhism across Central Asia.
Answer in a phrase: (a) Where is Kuchi? (b) Why is it famous?
questions.answer: (a) In Central Asia. (b) It was a flourishing centre of Indian culture where the Silk Route divided.

questions.q: Mark true or false: (a) Angkor Vat has scenes of Ramayana and Mahabharata. (b) Prambanan is a Buddhist temple.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False – it is a Shiva temple.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: The Arabs called Indian mathematics ______. They admired the decimal system with ______.
Answer in a phrase: (a) Name the two Indian astronomical works taken to Baghdad. (b) Who translated Sushruta Samhita into Arabic?
Mark true or false: (a) Yavanas guarded Tamil kings' tents. (b) India imported pepper and spices from Rome.
Fill in the blanks: Thailand was called ______ before 1939. ______ is the capital with 400 temples.
Answer in a phrase: (a) What was Suvarnadvipa? (b) Which Andhra king issued a ship coin?
questions.answer: (a) Java, Sumatra and Malaya (the golden islands). (b) Yajnasri.

questions.q: Mark true or false: (a) Bali still follows Hindu culture. (b) The Kawi script is based on Kharoshthi.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False – it is based on Brahmi.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in about 25 words.

questions.q: What was the most remarkable feature of the spread of Indian culture abroad?
questions.answer: It was not by conquest or threat but by voluntary acceptance of India's cultural and spiritual values.

questions.q: What is the importance of universities in the spread of Indian culture abroad?
questions.answer: Universities like Nalanda, Taxila, Vikramashila and Odantapuri attracted foreign students and teachers who carried Indian knowledge and religion abroad.

questions.q: Name two universities from ancient India.
Who was Thonmi Sambhota?
questions.answer: A Tibetan minister sent by King Naradeva who studied at Nalanda, devised the Tibetan script from Brahmi and wrote a grammar based on Panini.

questions.q: Who were the Romas?
questions.answer: Groups of Indian wanderers, known as Gypsies in Europe, who went west and kept their language, customs and music.

questions.q: What was the contribution of Bodhidharma?
questions.answer: He went from Kanchipuram to China with yoga and dhyana (ch'an) and is worshipped in China and Japan.

questions.q: Name two countries of South-East Asia influenced by Indian culture and one evidence.
questions.answer: Cambodia (Angkor Vat) and Indonesia (Prambanan temple); also Sanskrit inscriptions.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 40–50 words.

questions.q: Explain the place of Sanskrit in ancient Japanese society.
questions.answer: Sanskrit was accepted as the sacred language; monks were trained to write its syllables and mantras in the Shittan (Siddham) script; Buddhist sutras reached Japan through China and Korea.

or.q: Explain the place of Sanskrit in today's Japan.
or.answer: Japanese scholars still keenly study Sanskrit as the language of Buddhist scriptures, a cementing force between India and Japan.

questions.q: Describe three facts about the University of Odantapuri.
questions.answer: It was in Bihar; it grew in stature under the Pala kings; many monks migrated from it and settled in Tibet, where a monastery was founded on its model (by Jnanabhadra).

or.q: Describe the contributions of Acharya Kamalashila.
or.answer: He was a scholar of Nalanda invited by the king of Tibet to spread Buddhism; after his death the Tibetans embalmed his body and kept it in a monastery in Lhasa.

questions.q: Explain the efforts of King Naradeva of Tibet to promote Buddhism in his country.
questions.answer: He sent his minister Thonmi Sambhota with sixteen scholars to study in Magadha under Indian teachers; they brought books, devised the Tibetan script and grammar, and translated Sanskrit texts; the king himself studied the texts for four years.

or.q: Explain the works of Thonmi Sambhota in the field of education and in the development of the Tibetan script.
or.answer: He devised a new Tibetan script from Brahmi in the 7th century, wrote a grammar based on Panini and started the translation of Sanskrit books, ninety-six thousand of which were translated into Tibetan.

questions.q: Describe India's contacts with the Roman Empire.
questions.answer: In the first three centuries AD, South India had profitable sea trade with Rome, exporting pepper, spices, gems, pearls, ivory, silk and muslin; Roman coins were found at Coimbatore and Madurai; trade brought gold and gave the Kushanas a stable gold currency; yavanas guarded Tamil kings and ports at Sopara, Broach and Kaveripattinam handled the trade.

questions.q: Describe India's cultural contact with the Arab civilisation.
questions.answer: Indian astronomy books (Brahmasphutasiddhanta, Khandakhadyaka) were translated at Baghdad; Arabs adopted the decimal system and zero and called mathematics hindisa; Indian medical works including the Sushruta Samhita were translated at Harun al-Rashid's behest; Arabic shipping words came from Indian words.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 150–200 words.

questions.q: Examine the role of traders and explorers in extending Indian outreach to far-off countries.
questions.answer: Traders from Kashi, Mathura, Ujjain, Prayag and Pataliputra and east coast ports like Mamallapuram, Tamralipti and Kaveripattinam travelled to Rome, China, and from the 1st century BC to Java, Sumatra, Malaya and Cambodia in search of gold (Suvarnadvipa). Kalinga traded with Sri Lanka under Ashoka. Wherever they went they established cultural links and became cultural ambassadors; Indian navigators sailed under the Guptas and Cholas; the Silk Route carried Buddhism; Indians learnt silk-making, gold coinage and betel growing in return.

or.q: How did Indian culture spread in far-flung countries during the ancient period?
or.answer: By traders, teachers, emissaries and missionaries, by universities such as Nalanda, by the Silk Route and sea routes, by Buddhism and Sanskrit and by migrants like the Romas; it was by voluntary acceptance.

questions.q: Describe the spread of Indian culture in South-East Asia (Cambodia, Thailand and Indonesia).
questions.answer: Cambodia: Indian-origin Kaundinya kings, Sanskrit inscriptions and administration up to the 14th century, Hindu polity, Angkor Vat with Ramayana and Mahabharata scenes and the Samudra Manthan. Thailand: Sanskrit names for kingdoms and cities, Vishnu images, Ayutthaya (Ayodhya), 400 temples in Bangkok. Indonesia: Prambanan Shiva temple, Ramayana and Krishna stories on walls, Bali's Hindu culture and Sanskrit hymns, Kawi script from Brahmi and the Wayang shadow play.

questions.q: Discuss the role of ancient universities, teachers and missionaries in spreading Indian culture abroad.
questions.answer: Nalanda (with a seven-storey library), Valabhi, Vikramashila and Odantapuri drew students from China, Tibet and Korea. Kashyapa Matanga and Dharmarakshita went to China in AD 67, Kumarajiva translated Sanskrit texts into Chinese, Bodhidharma popularised dhyana, Kamalashila, Jnanabhadra and Atisha taught in Tibet and Thonmi Sambhota devised the Tibetan script. Students and teachers carried knowledge and religion; Ashoka's children Mahendra and Sanghamitra took Buddhism to Sri Lanka.

questions.q: Explain how Buddhism and Indian culture spread to China, Korea and Japan.
questions.answer: Indian monks Kashyapa Matanga and Dharmarakshita went to China (AD 67) on Ming Ti's invitation; the Wei emperor made Buddhism the state religion; thousands of Sanskrit books were translated and cave temples were built at Dunhuang, Yungang and Longmen. Through China, Sundo took Buddhism to Korea in AD 352 and dhyana yoga came in the 8th–9th century. In AD 552 Korea sent a Buddha statue, sutras and artists to Japan, where Buddhism became the state religion and Sanskrit a sacred language written in the Shittan script.

questions.q: Discuss the trade of ancient India with the Roman Empire and the Arabs.
questions.answer: South India had profitable sea trade with the Roman Empire in the first three centuries AD, exporting pepper, spices, gems, pearls, ivory, silk and muslin; this brought gold, a stable currency to the Kushanas, ports like Sopara and Kaveripattinam and Roman coins at Coimbatore and Madurai; Pliny deplored the drain of gold. Arab traders and travellers recorded flourishing commerce from the mid-9th century; India gave the Arabs astronomy, the decimal system with zero (hindisa) and medicine.
